column1: # Raw term frequencies harvested from 60 US patents (C11B 9/00 + A61Q 13/00), 4.64M chars.
# Method: words immediately preceding an odour-head noun (odour|note|character|aroma|nuance),
#         minus a generic English/patent stop list. NOT hand-supplied — corpus-derived.
# Retrieved 2026-08-01. 1,035 distinct terms; only 14 occur >=30 times at this corpus size.
# This is RAW. It is not the ontology. Classification below is a first human pass and is
#   D  = plausible odour descriptor        -> ontology candidate
#   H  = hedonic (pleasant/unpleasant)     -> not a descriptor, may be a separate axis
#   T  = note-tier / positional vocabulary -> see handrun-04: NOT per-compound assertable
#   M  = malodour context (deodorant patents) -> signals a document to exclude
